title: ～なきゃいけない
shortExplanation: Express a necessity or obligation; 'must', 'have to'.
longExplanation: The ～なきゃいけない grammar point is used to express a sense of necessity or obligation, similar to saying 'must' or 'have to' in English. It is a casual and more colloquial form of the ～なければいけない grammar point. The formation is different for verbs, but it is not used with い-adjectives, な-adjectives, or nouns.
formation: Verb-casual (negative form without い) + なきゃいけない

examples.jp: 明日までに宿題を終わらなきゃいけない。
examples.romaji: Ashita made ni shukudai wo owaranakya ikenai.
examples.en: I have to finish my homework by tomorrow.

examples.jp: もうすぐ出かけるから、急いで準備しなきゃいけない。
examples.romaji: Mou sugu dekakeru kara, isoide junbi shinakya ikenai.
examples.en: We're leaving soon, so I have to hurry and get ready.

examples.jp: このプロジェクトは来週提出しなきゃいけない。
examples.romaji: Kono purojekuto wa raishuu teishutsu shinakya ikenai.
examples.en: I must submit this project by next week.

examples.jp: 電車に乗る前に、切符を買わなきゃいけない。
examples.romaji: Densha ni noru mae ni, kippu wo kawanakya ikenai.
examples.en: I have to buy a ticket before getting on the train.

usageNote: Casual contraction (なければ→なきゃ); the most common everyday spoken form.
